headline: Revenue climbs, but merger costs and taxes hit profit
summary_short: Revenue rose 14.9% year-over-year to $390.0 million on continued thrombectomy and embolization/access growth, but net income fell 23% to $34.8 million as acquisition-related costs and a much higher effective tax rate (24.6% vs 0.1% a year ago) weighed on the bottom line.
summary_long: Q2 FY26 revenue rose 14.9% y/y to $390.0M on higher thrombectomy (+12.5%) and embolization/access (+20.0%) sales from greater U.S. market penetration; gross margin expanded 190bp to 67.9% on favorable product mix. R&D rose 9.4% to $25.4M; SG&A rose 24.1% to $198.5M, including $6.9M of costs tied to the pending Boston Scientific merger plus higher personnel and marketing spend. Net income fell 23% to $34.8M and diluted EPS fell to $0.88 from $1.15, mainly on the effective tax rate rising to 24.6% from 0.1%. Six-month operating cash flow was $133.1M, up from $93.9M; cash fell to $205.3M from $421.8M as funds shifted into marketable investments and Costa Rica capex continued. No standalone forward guidance was issued given the pending merger.
confidence_notes: Force-regenerate run per operator instruction, overwriting any prior state on disk for this period; treat this as a fresh compose, not an incremental update. Penumbra is subject to a pending acquisition by Boston Scientific Corporation (Merger Agreement dated 2026-01-14; $374.00/share cash-or-stock, ~$14.5B enterprise value; expected to close in 2026 subject to regulatory approval) — this materially shapes the quarter: SG&A includes $6.9M (Q2) / $16.4M (H1) of acquisition-related professional-services costs, and the company has stated it will not issue full-year 2026 guidance or hold an earnings call while the deal is pending. Revenue, gross profit, operating income, EBIT and EBITDA KPIs carry Yahoo fundamentals-timeseries provenance in the shard; EPS, cost of revenue, pretax income, cash and equity carry SEC-XBRL regulatory provenance from this same 10-Q. The two sources reconcile exactly (e.g. shard revenue $390.046M vs the filing's own stated $390.0 million, +14.9% y/y). The y/y net income and EPS decline is almost entirely a tax-rate effect: effective tax rate rose to 24.6% (Q2) from an immaterial 0.1% a year earlier, which the filing attributes to a decrease in excess tax benefits from stock-based compensation in the U.S. jurisdiction — pretax income was actually up 1.9% y/y ($46.2M vs $45.3M). No dividend, and no share repurchases occurred this quarter (remaining $100.0M buyback authorization unchanged from the prior period).
